# BDPM Site Services

BDPM Site Services is an excavation contractor in Plymouth, MA specializing in site construction and excavation, septic system installation, Title 5 inspections, sea walls and helical piers.

- Service Area: Plymouth, MA and the surrounding area (Plymouth Center, North Plymouth, West Plymouth, South Plymouth, Manomet, Cedarville)

## Services
- Site Construction / Excavation: foundation digs, grading and trenches planned around Dig Safe, ledge and wetlands
- Septic System Installation: systems built to the approved Board of Health design, from soil test to backfill inspection
- Title 5 Inspections: Massachusetts Title 5 septic inspections for home sales
- Sea Walls: sea wall construction for Plymouth waterfront property, planned around the coastal bank, the tides and Conservation Commission permits
- Helical Piers: pier installation for new foundations, additions, decks and porches

## About
BDPM Site Services is owned by Patrick Howard and based at 168 Beaver Dam Rd in Plymouth, MA. It handles five kinds of ground work for residential and commercial properties. A job starts with a site visit and a written estimate that states the scope, price and schedule. Dig Safe (811) notice and any Plymouth Conservation Commission or Board of Health review come before digging.


## Full About
BDPM Site Services is an excavation contractor owned by Patrick Howard at 168 Beaver Dam Rd in Plymouth, MA 02360. Its five services are all ground work, so one contractor can handle the dig, the septic system and the support underneath it. It takes on residential and commercial properties in Plymouth. Plymouth lots vary from sandy and gravelly soils to clay, fill and exposed ledge, and much of the town sits near wetlands or the coast, so most jobs involve a Dig Safe notice and some form of town review.

## Service Details
### Site Construction / Excavation
Foundation digs, grading and trenches in Plymouth, planned around Dig Safe, ledge and wetlands. Pricing depends on the size of the job, soil and ledge conditions, site access, how much material must be hauled away, and the timeline. BDPM Site Services gives a written estimate after a site visit, with the scope, price and schedule spelled out. Page: https://bdpm-site-services.pageone.cloud/services/site-construction-excavation/

### Septic System Installation
A Plymouth septic installation starts with a soil test and a design from a licensed professional, approved by the Board of Health before any digging. BDPM Site Services builds to that approved plan, and the town inspects the system before it is backfilled. Page: https://bdpm-site-services.pageone.cloud/services/septic-system-installation/

### Title 5 Inspections
A Title 5 inspection is required before most Massachusetts property transfers that involve a septic system. It must be done within two years before the sale, or within three years if the tank has been pumped every year and the records are kept. Page: https://bdpm-site-services.pageone.cloud/services/title-5-inspections/

### Sea Walls
A new sea wall at a coastal bank is allowed only in specific cases in Massachusetts, mainly to protect a building built before August 10, 1978, and the Plymouth Conservation Commission reviews the project. BDPM Site Services looks at the shoreline during the estimate and explains what review is likely. Page: https://bdpm-site-services.pageone.cloud/services/sea-walls/

### Helical Piers
A helical pier is a steel shaft with helical plates that is screwed into the ground until it reaches firm soil. It is the better choice than a concrete footing when the soil at footing depth is loose, wet or old fill, when access is tight, or when the job cannot wait for concrete to cure. Page: https://bdpm-site-services.pageone.cloud/services/helical-piers/

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do I need to call Dig Safe before digging in Plymouth?
A: Yes. In Massachusetts, you must contact Dig Safe by calling 811 or 1-888-344-7233 before any excavation, and utility companies then mark their underground lines. Dig Safe requires notice at least 72 hours before digging, not counting weekends and holidays.

Q: Will my project need a wetlands or conservation permit in Plymouth?
A: It may. Work within wetland resource areas or their buffer zones is regulated under the Massachusetts Wetlands Protection Act and local bylaws, which often means review by the Plymouth Conservation Commission.

Q: How much does excavation cost in Plymouth?
A: Excavation pricing depends on the size of the job, soil and ledge conditions, site access, how much material must be hauled away, and the timeline. BDPM Site Services gives a written estimate after a site visit, with the scope, price and schedule spelled out.

Q: What does a written estimate from BDPM Site Services include?
A: A written estimate from BDPM Site Services states the scope of work, the price and the schedule, based on what the site visit found about soil, ledge, access and water.

Q: What happens during an excavation job, from first call to final grade?
A: A BDPM Site Services job has four steps: a site visit, a written estimate, Dig Safe and any approvals, then the dig, build and grade. The work is inspected where required, and the site is left at final grade.

Q: Do I need a septic design before BDPM Site Services can install a system?
A: Yes. A Plymouth septic installation starts with a soil test and a design from a licensed professional, approved by the Board of Health before any digging.

Q: When is a Title 5 inspection required in Massachusetts?
A: Before most property transfers that involve a septic system. It must be done within two years before the sale, or within three years if the tank has been pumped every year and the records are kept.

Q: What types of soil and site conditions does BDPM Site Services deal with?
A: Plymouth sites vary widely, from sandy and gravelly soils to clay, fill and exposed ledge. Each site is assessed during the estimate so the right equipment, drainage and disposal plan are included in the quote before work begins.

Q: What are the office hours and how do I reach BDPM Site Services?
A: Mon-Fri 7am-5pm, Sat-Sun closed. Call (508) 989-7101 or email patrick@bdpmma.com.
